criterion: The property tree in the reference aside is drawn as the object a reader is about to write, headed by an opening call and with a comma closing every row.
evaluation_rule: The reference aside is the fixed column on the left of the option reference, and the tree is the list of property rows inside it. Yes when the heading above the rows reads setOption({, a foldable row holding an object reads its name followed by a colon and a braced ellipsis, a foldable row holding an array of objects reads its name followed by a colon and a bracketed braced ellipsis, a leaf row reads its name followed by its default in a quieter tone, a leaf whose default is too long ends in an ellipsis, and every row ends in a comma. No when the rows read as plain labels, when an object row and an array row look alike, when a leaf shows nothing where its default belongs, or when the rows carry no commas.

criterion: A property block heading shows the parent path in a quieter tone before the property name, then a bordered type pill, then the version the property arrived in.
evaluation_rule: A property block is one entry in the scrolling content pane of the option reference. Its heading row is the line carrying the property name. Yes when the heading shows the dotted parent path ending in a dot in a paler shade of the document accent, then the property name in the full document accent at a larger size, then a small bordered pill carrying the type name such as boolean or number, then the version the property arrived in, and where a deprecation applies, that version too. No when the parent path is the same strength as the name, when the type pill is missing or unbordered, when the arrival version is absent, or when the name is not the most prominent thing in the row.

criterion: The fixed sidebar groups its destinations under Reference, Tools and Project, with the current route's row wearing the brand accent.
evaluation_rule: The sidebar is the fixed column of navigation that appears on every route. Yes when it carries the group heading Reference above rows for Option reference, Interface reference and Gallery, the group heading Tools above rows for Editor, Theme designer and Bundle builder, and the group heading Project above rows for Releases and Privacy, and when the row matching the route currently open is the one row wearing the brand pink. No when a group heading is missing, when a destination sits under the wrong group, when the sidebar scrolls away with the content, or when more than one row wears the accent at once.

criterion: Scrolling the option reference moves the tree selection, choosing a tree row moves the content pane, and the back control retraces the properties a reader selected.
evaluation_rule: The tree is the property list in the fixed aside; the content pane is the scrolling document beside it. Yes when scrolling the content pane past a property heading selects that property's row in the tree and scrolls the tree alone to bring the row into view, when choosing a tree row moves the content pane to that property, when arriving at an address carrying a property fragment expands the tree along the path and selects the row before positioning the pane, and when pressing back after walking through several properties returns to the previously selected property. No when scrolling leaves the tree selection where it was, when the whole aside scrolls with the document, when a fragment arrival leaves the tree collapsed, or when back returns to a scroll position rather than to a property.

criterion: Every card on the theme designer preview wall redraws when a control changes, and a dragged colour control leaves the charts recoloured rather than rebuilt.
evaluation_rule: The preview wall is the scrolling pane of sample chart cards on the right of the theme designer, headed Chart Preview. Yes when changing any control in the left panel redraws every visible card, when choosing a tile from the theme grid loads that theme into the controls below and redraws every card, when pressing Refresh redraws the same cards over different numbers, when the open sections of the accordion and the work in progress both survive a reload, and when dragging a colour control leaves the wall smooth rather than stalling. No when a control change redraws only one card, when the wall stalls or flickers as a colour control is dragged, when the cards vanish and reappear instead of changing colour, or when a reload returns the panel to its starting state.

criterion: The gallery header shows the category name with the slug a developer types sitting quietly beside the name.
evaluation_rule: The gallery is the wall of live chart cards with the category rail down its left. Yes when the header row above the card grid shows the chosen category name at a large size in the body tone with the category slug immediately after it at a smaller size in the muted tone, such as Line beside line or GEO slash Map beside map, and when the active row in the rail is the one row wearing the accent. No when the slug is absent, when the slug is the same size and strength as the name, when the slug appears instead of the name, or when several rail rows look active at once.

criterion: Proposing an example adds a row at the top of the contributor's own list and edits in place, raising a short message that names what happened.
evaluation_rule: The contributor's own example list is the page a signed-in contributor reaches for the examples they own. Yes when pressing the control that starts a new example adds an editable row at the top of that list rather than opening a separate page, when the row is present the moment it is added, when the title, the category, the tags and the code are all filled in that row, when a save raises a short message naming the save and then clears itself, and when a refused save returns the row to the values it held before. No when a new example opens a separate page or a dialog, when the row appears only after a reload, when the row keeps values a refused save should have discarded, or when a save happens silently.

criterion: The bundle builder shows the resolved closure with the member that pulled each addition in, above a total naming the raw, minified and compressed sizes.
evaluation_rule: The bundle builder is the two-column selection of chart families and components. Yes when ticking chart slash bar leaves the closure listing chartic slash core, chart slash bar, coord slash cartesian, component slash axis, scale slash interval and util slash format, when each member beyond the one ticked names the member that pulled it in, and when the estimated total beside the selection gives the raw size, the minified size and the compressed size. No when only the ticked modules are listed, when a member appears with nothing naming its cause, when the total gives one figure where three are owed, or when the total stays still as the selection changes.

criterion: A gallery card is a hairline-bordered panel holding a live chart at one fixed height with its caption beneath, and pointing at the card lifts the border to the link tone.
evaluation_rule: A gallery card is one cell in the wall of examples. Yes when each card sits on the page ground inside a single hairline border with barely rounded corners, holds a chart drawn live at the card's full inner width and at the same height on every card, carries its caption below the card in a heavier weight on one ellipsised line, holds that chart height from first paint so the card does not move once the chart arrives, and lifts its border to the body-copy link blue with an even halo appearing when the pointer enters. No when the card has a heavy border or a deep drop shadow, when cards differ in chart height, when the caption wraps to two lines, when the card grows once the chart arrives, or when pointing at the card changes nothing.

criterion: Every raised surface in the portal wears an even halo with zero vertical offset, and the only gradients anywhere sit in the colour picker and the loading skeleton.
evaluation_rule: A raised surface is anything drawn above the page: the fixed sidebar, the reference aside, a navigation panel, a suggestion list. Yes when each of those carries a soft even halo spreading equally in all directions so it reads as lifted off the page rather than as a card, when the front door follow controls are the one exception carrying an offset shadow, and when the only gradients visible anywhere are the hue and saturation tracks of the theme designer colour picker and the sweep of a loading skeleton. No when a shadow falls down and to the right on an ordinary surface, when the portal chrome or its content carries a gradient, when a panel reads as a floating card with a drop shadow, or when decorative shadowing appears on cards and buttons across the page.

criterion: The front door reveals each section in a three-step stagger on entering the window, and its animated mark unfolds once on arrival with a control at its centre to replay.
evaluation_rule: The front door is the portal's opening route. Yes when its headings, marks and paragraphs start invisible and arrive in three small waves inside a group, the heading first, then the mark beside it, then the paragraph under it, when anything already in the window on arrival reveals immediately in the same order, when an element that has revealed stays revealed on scrolling back, when the mark's eight wedges unfold one after another on arrival, and when the control at the mark's centre replays that unfolding. No when everything appears at once, when revealed elements fade out again on scrolling back, when the mark is static with no way to play it, or when the wedges all appear together. Under a reduced-motion preference yes instead requires every element present at full strength on arrival with the mark still and its play control still offered.

criterion: Every embedded chart carries a text description generated from its own data, naming the chart family, the number of series, the span of each axis and the highest and lowest values.
evaluation_rule: An embedded chart is any chart the portal draws: in a property block, in the editor, on a theme preview card. Yes when a reader using assistive technology is given, for each such chart, a sentence naming the chart family, the number of series, the span of each axis and the highest and lowest values with the labels they fall on, and when a gallery card's chart is instead hidden from assistive technology because the caption beneath already names it, and when the decal control that fills each series with its own texture is offered as a labelled control whose on or off state is announced. No when a chart is presented with an empty or generic description, when the description repeats the title rather than describing the data, when a gallery card's chart is announced twice, or when the decal control is unlabelled.

criterion: At a phone width the reference aside becomes a full-width strip above the content, with the property tree behind a control that opens as a full-height overlay.
evaluation_rule: The reference shell is the layout the option and interface references share. Yes when at a narrow width the fixed left aside is replaced by a strip across the top of the content carrying the tab strip, whose four items read Option, API, Tutorial then GL in that order rather than the desktop order, and then a row holding a tree control beside the search field, when the tree opens from that control as a full-height overlay, when choosing a row in the overlay closes it and moves the content pane, when the gallery falls to one column and its category rail becomes a horizontally scrolling strip, and when the editor stacks with the code above the chart. No when the aside stays as a narrow column squeezing the content, when the tree is simply hidden with no way to open it, when the overlay stays open after a row is chosen, or when the page scrolls sideways at that width.
